app/static/style.css — the stylesheet

Purpose

The single self-contained stylesheet for the UI: the design tokens (custom properties on :root), the application-frame layout (app header, left-pane navigation, view panes, and the narrow-viewport collapse), and the class styles for every region app.js drives. No web fonts, no CDN, no external references of any kind — the app's no-CDN constraint applies to CSS as firmly as to JS.

Public surface

Design tokens: --bg, --panel, --text, --muted, --accent, --accent-dark, --error-*, --border. Class/element contract with index.html / app.js: .container (the single 760px column), .header / .header-row, .row, .url-input, .btn / .btn-quiet, .spinner, .error-banner, .result-*, .video-title, .video-language, .transcript-panel, .provider-picker, .auto-summarize-label (the checkbox label; dims with the input's :disabled via :has()), .auto-note (the muted auto-summarize failure note), .summary-*, .saved-* (.saved-row is the button-styled list item), .injection-panel / .injection-controls (the benchmark panel and its flex control row), .injection-toggle-label (dims with the toggle's :disabled via :has()), .injection-point / .difficulty-picker / .benchmark-judge (the single-select controls), .difficulty-error (the inline error status line), .benchmark-label, .benchmark-models (the multi-select), .injection-payload, .injection-preview (the dashed spliced-text preview), .benchmark-tally (the per-model results table), .benchmark-rows / .bench-row / .bench-row-title / .bench-output / .bench-meta / .bench-human-label / .bench-human (the per-model result rows), .log-panel, and the application frame: .app-header / .app-header-row / .app-brand (the brand + log-toggle row over the log panel), .app-body (the nav + main-pane row), .app-nav / .nav-item (the left navigation column; .nav-item.active is the active-view state), .app-main (the view-pane column), .view (a view section), #view-docs / .docs-toolbar / #docs-frame (the Docs view: a toolbar row over an iframe that fills the remaining pane height).

Invariants

  • Self-contained. No @import, no web fonts, no external URLs; the font stacks are the system stack for text and ui-monospace/Menlo/Consolas for the log panel and transcript pre blocks.
  • [hidden] { display: none !important; } is load-bearing. It keeps the hidden attribute authoritative even for styled elements (buttons and panels with display rules), so app.js's visibility contract can never be silently defeated by a class — including the #view-docs section, which has its own display: flex rule but must stay invisible while hidden.
  • The page is a full-height flex column: app header, then the nav + main-pane row. body is display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 100vh, so the frame fills the viewport when content is short while long Transcripts content still grows the page. .app-body is a row (display: flex) whose .app-nav is a fixed 200px column and whose .app-main is the flexing view-pane column.
  • The Docs view's iframe fills the main pane. #view-docs is a flex column; the toolbar owns the top strip and #docs-frame is flex: 1; min-height: 0, so the iframe takes the pane's full width and remaining height and gives the docs their own scroll context.
  • Narrow viewports collapse the nav to a horizontal tab row. At @media (max-width: 800px) (mirroring the docs' own breakpoint) .app-body becomes a column and .app-nav a full-width row of equal (flex: 1) centered items above the content, so a 420px viewport shows no horizontal overflow.
  • The app header is a column of rows (.app-header, flex-direction: column, align-items: stretch): brand + log toggle in the first row (.app-header-row, space-between), the log panel as the second row. Spacing between rows comes from the column's gap, not from the panel's margin-top — the panel sits close beneath the toggle when opened and contributes no height when hidden. The Transcripts view keeps its own slim .header (title + subtitle only) beneath it.
  • Every long region scrolls internally with a bounded height: the transcript panel max-height: 60vh, the summary text and saved list 40vh, the log panel 40vh, the injection spliced-text preview 30vh — opening any of them never grows the page without bound.
  • Buttons are keyboard- and state-honest: .btn:disabled dims and forbids; .saved-row keeps :focus-visible outlines; hover states apply only to :not(:disabled).
  • Long content wraps, never overflows: overflow-wrap: anywhere on titles, transcript, saved names, and the log panel.

Design decisions

Resolved from the archived change design docs:

  • 2026-10-29-youtube-transcript D6 — the no-build, no-CDN front-end constraint this file obeys.
  • 2026-11-02-add-saved-transcript-list decision 6 — the saved section's treatment: bounded scrollable <ul> matching the existing .transcript-panel treatment, button-styled rows, the cosmetic text-transform: capitalize on .saved-name (accepted trade-off: acronym-like words are lowercased cosmetically; the real name is always what is requested and downloaded).
  • 2026-11-06-move-log-panel-into-header D2/D3 — the column-of-rows header (align-items: stretch so rows span the full width) and the row-gap spacing that replaced the old .log-panel { margin: 32px 0 0; }.
  • add-prompt-injection-benchmark decision 1 and decision 5 — the injection-benchmark panel's treatment: the flex control row, the bounded spliced-text preview, and the per-model tally table + result rows that the layered oracle (canary/judge/human) populates, all following the existing region conventions (bounded scroll, keyboard/state-honest controls).
  • benchmark-difficulty-picker decision 4 — the difficulty select and re-roll join the control row reusing the existing classes, and the .difficulty-error status line is a muted inline failure note (hidden except on failure), not the error banner.
  • add-docs-view D3 (the Docs view: the toolbar row over #docs-frame, which fills the main pane height so the docs get their own scroll context), D4 (the app-level frame: the full-height flex-column body, the 200px left nav column beside the flexing main pane, the brand + log viewer in the app header), and D6 (the @media (max-width: 800px) collapse of the nav into a horizontal tab row, mirroring the docs' own narrow-layout breakpoint and keeping the 420px overflow contract green).
